subject: Probably a glitch in calculating DIC for time series at irregular time points?

messages.author: c8fc4bff1d6a3efd
messages.subject: Probably a glitch in calculating DIC for time series at irregular time points?
parts:
I got the following error message from R-INLA:

Error in numeric(n.fam) : vector size cannot be infinite
In addition: Warning message:
In max(f.idx, na.rm = TRUE) :
  no non-missing arguments to max; returning -Inf


From the following code
library(INLA)
library(BayesianAnimalTracker)

###To get the data out and preparation
data("Trip1DR")
data("Trip1GPS")
Trip1GPSformat <- GPStable(Trip1GPS)
Trip1GPSinKM <- DegToKM(Trip1GPSformat)
T <- nrow(Trip1DR)
ndl <- as.dataList(Trip1DR$Xdim/1000, Trip1GPSinKM$Northing, 
                   Ytime=strptime(Trip1GPSinKM$DateTime, "%d-%b-%Y %H:%M:%S"), 
                   Xtime=strptime(Trip1DR$DateTime, "%d-%b-%Y %H:%M:%S"), 
                   s2G=0.0625, timeUnit=1, betaOrder=1)
#This function just calculated the time steps and matches the time points.

Y <- rep(NA, T)
Y[ndl$g$gind] <- ndl$g$Y
X <- ndl$XMx[,1]
Time <- ndl$XMx[,2]

mod <- Y~ X + f(Time1, model="rw1") + f(Time2, aX, model="rw1")
 #Y = a + bX + rw1 + (another rw1)*X + epsilon

rLat <- inla(mod, data=list(Y=Y, X=X, Time1=Time, Time2=Time, aX=X),
family="gaussian", verbose=TRUE, control.compute=list(dic=TRUE))


The code works fine without the "control.compute=list(dic=TRUE)" part, or okay (but it is a wrong model) if I replace Time by 1:T.

So I guess there is a glitch in the computation of the DIC. I am not quite sure if there is other ways to get around this problem.

Could you help me with it?

Thank you very much.
Cheers, 
Seagle
